data.title: You Were Once Smarter Than AI at Math. Yes, Even You. — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Cohen | Development by Jason French

Before math changed forever, researchers inside OpenAI reported a monumental breakthrough: AI was nearly as smart as a bunch of kids in elementary school.

Five years ago, the engineers on the frontier of artificial intelligence trained a model to solve thousands of basic math problems. Then they put it to the test. Now it's your turn.

Pop quiz! (Or just keep reading.)

Even if you're allergic to math, you can probably handle this simple arithmetic. As OpenAI's researchers put it: "A bright middle-school student should be able to solve every problem."

But what about a student in elementary school — or an AI model?

When the company gave this exam to a group of kids between the ages of nine and 12, they scored 60%. The primitive AI system was given the same test and scored 55%. And the researchers were elated.

"I still remember the feeling of jumping up and down," OpenAI chief research officer Mark Chen told me, "for things that we would laugh at now."

Never had a failing grade on a math exam felt so good. At the time, the models were lousy at reasoning through problems step by step. Since then, AI has become more powerful in far less time than even the researchers expected.

It's no longer struggling to do fourth-grade homework. Now it's doing mathematics that no human has ever done.

In the past few weeks alone, an OpenAI internal model solved one of the legendary Millennium Prize Problems and then several hundred more open problems, which seemed inconceivable even a few months ago. This explosion of discoveries has left the field reeling — proof that math will never be the same.

Math has become the easiest way to understand how dramatically AI's capabilities have advanced and how badly people have underestimated them. So now what? If the models went from being stumped by long division to cracking the quasi-Riemann hypothesis in five years, how will the next five years play out? And if AI can master a field that turns most of our brains to mush, is it only a matter of time before it comes for the rest of us?

These are much harder questions than counting unicorns and Janet's egg sales — and mathematicians didn't think they would have to answer them first. Not long ago, in fact, math was thought to be one of the last fields AI would transform.

But as the companies used math to train their models, those models became much, much better at math.

In 2023, OpenAI's top model breezed through the grade-school math exam that previous machines had flunked. That rapid improvement meant it was ready for a more grueling test of mathematical knowledge.

It was time for AI to take the SAT.

The model scored 700 of 800 on the SAT's math section — a sign of how far these systems had come and how far they still had to go. Even then, AI was outperformed by teenagers who would go to college and major in English so they wouldn't have to think about algebra.

Around this time, AI tools were still famously bad at answering one math question that wouldn't appear on any standardized test: How many r's are in the word strawberry? (Hint: not two.)

But inside the labs, researchers could see that the next generation of models wouldn't have any trouble computing the number of letters in fruit.

AI went from not working very well to working so well it's scary partly because of the nature of math itself. Unlike messier domains, math has been governed by precise rules of logic for millennia. It's also verifiable. Answers are right or wrong, so models can learn from their mistakes, just like 9-year-olds.

Next up in their math education: problems from the high-school competitions that many AI researchers had once entered themselves.

At first, the models stumbled on tricky problems that required complex multistep reasoning. But like other math benchmark tests, this one would eventually get obliterated.

In mid-2023, OpenAI's top model scored 23% on the test's hardest problems. In 2024, the company rolled out its first reasoning model — code-named "Strawberry" — and it was particularly strong in math and coding. By the end of 2024, OpenAI's signature model hit 95% on that exam.

And in early 2025, that progress became personal for OpenAI's research leader.

When he was informed the models had surpassed his peak rating as a competitive programmer, Chen suddenly empathized with Lee Sedol, one of the world's top Go players, who was defeated by AlphaGo in a defining event of AI history.

"That was a real emotional moment for me," he said. "I feel like people who have undergone moments like that have a greater appreciation for what the models are able to do in the future."

Chen had another reason to appreciate their perfect score on the notoriously difficult American Invitational Mathematics Examination. When he was a high-school senior, 8,586 students from all over the world took the AIME. Nine got perfect scores. He was one of them.

Once the AI models aced the AIME and won gold medals at the math Olympics, they graduated from high-school math to open problems whose solutions had eluded humans for decades.

I asked Chen what he would have said if I had told him in 2021 about the velocity of the next five years.

"I would have said that's crazy," he said. "But the harsh lesson here is that people are really bad at internalizing exponentials — even people inside OpenAI."

When I called Scott Aaronson and Dana Moshkovitz, a married couple of theoretical computer scientists at the University of Texas, I learned why it's so hard to predict the pace of progress.

"Things happen faster than you expect," Aaronson said, "even when you update on the last thing happening faster than you expected."

In the before times otherwise known as August 2026, Moshkovitz was talking with a colleague about the Unique Games Conjecture, a highly abstract problem that had occupied her mind for more than a decade. When she floated the idea that AI might solve it one day, the suggestion was so preposterous that he thought she was joking. Two months later, she was proven right when the solution appeared in OpenAI's blizzard of papers.

Moshkovitz broke the news to her son when she picked him up from school. As it happens, he is 9 years old — the same age as the youngest participants in OpenAI's study.

They are no longer smarter than AI at solving math problems, but 9-year-olds are still pretty wise.

"He told me," Moshkovitz said, "they should solve cancer instead."

data.title: Stocktwits Weekly Spread: What Shaped Treasury Yields And The Dollar This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • An AI-linked equities basket (SOX) dropped, and the Nasdaq 100 capped its worst two-week decline since April 2025; investors poured into U.S. Treasuries, driving the 10-year yield back below 5.00%.
  • The U.S. Dollar Index eased marginally, down 0.2%, this week.
  • The yield curve flattened further this week, with 10-year yields falling about 8 basis points over the previous week.

U.S. government bonds staged a powerful rally during the week ending October 23, as a sharp retreat in artificial intelligence tech stocks and rising corporate credit risks sparked a major flight-to-quality rotation into fixed income.

The sudden reversal reflects growing investor anxiety regarding the hundreds of billions of dollars in corporate borrowing earmarked for AI computing infrastructure. Gartner warned this week that AI data center owners could face up to $4 trillion in asset write-down risks by 2032 if hyperscaler revenue fails to cover massive capital expenditure commitments.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell back below the 5.00% threshold for the first time in four weeks. The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield slipped 10 basis points from the previous week to 5.32% for the week ending Oct. 23.

The spread between the U.S. 10-year yield and the U.S. 2-year yield ticked lower to 0.31% in the week, from 0.37% a week ago.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF (TLT) ended the week 1.6% higher, while the shorter-duration iShares 1-3 year ETF (SHY) added about 0.2%. The slight recovery in the shorter-duration bond ETF may reflect easing short-term inflation pressure; however, markets still factor in one more rate hike in December.

Retail sentiment on TLT and SHY was ‘bullish,’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

Yield curve flattening trends persisted as short-duration yields eased more slowly than the long end, keeping the gap between 2-year and 10-year Treasuries tightly compressed.

Alternatively, corporate credit spreads widened, signaling growing stress in corporate balance sheets. Credit default swap prices on specialized "neocloud" providers and major AI hardware builders surged as markets questioned their ability to service burgeoning debt loads.

For instance, CoreWeave’s (CRWV) widening credit spreads pushed its stock to lose about 12% this week, its third straight weekly decline.

International sovereign bond markets followed similar trajectories. German 10-year Bund yields and other major sovereign yields mirrored the U.S. decline, reflecting broad-based global demand for safe-haven assets.

The Dollar Spot Index slipped 0.2% this week, extending last week’s weakness against a basket of developed market currencies.

data.title: Stocktwits Zero To Sixty: Tesla And SpaceX Form Merger Committees As Profits Drop, While Rivian Buys AI Startup And GM, Ford Advance EV Plans
data.description:
Key points:
  • Elon Musk said Tuesday that Tesla and SpaceX have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a potential merger.
  • Tesla executives said the company is aiming to begin delivering Cybercabs to external fleet customers by the end of 2026.
  • Rivian announced Thursday that it has acquired Third Dimension AI, a UK-based startup that turns real-world images and video into controllable 3D environments.

Tesla and SpaceX moved closer to a possible combination this week after Elon Musk publicly endorsed the idea, while the EV maker reported flat revenue and a profit decline for the third quarter.

Autonomy efforts advanced elsewhere, with Rivian acquiring a simulation startup and Lucid locking in European robotaxi software. GM detailed a lower-cost next-generation platform, and Ford refreshed the Mustang Mach-E.

Tesla And SpaceX Explore Combination; EV Giant’s Q3 Earnings Drop

Elon Musk said Tuesday that Tesla and his rocket manufacturing company SpaceX have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a potential merger.

On SpaceX’s quarterly earnings call, he described combining the companies as “a good idea” but said he has recused himself from the discussions because of conflicts of interest. Any deal would still require approval from both special committees, the respective boards, and shareholders. Talks remain at an early stage.

Tesla, meanwhile, reported revenue of $28 billion, compared to an analyst estimate of $28.3 billion, and adjusted earnings of $0.48 per share, against an expected EPS of $0.45, for the period ended September 30. Both revenue and earnings, however, dropped from the corresponding quarter of 2025.

Automotive revenue declined 3%, while energy generation and storage revenue fell 16%. Operating margin compressed amid continued heavy investment in AI, robotics, and autonomy, raising capital expenditure by 110% to $4.7 billion. The company, however, slashed its full-year capex estimate to $20 billion, down from the previously estimated $25 billion.

On Tesla’s earnings call, company executives said the company is aiming to begin delivering Cybercabs to external fleet customers by the end of 2026. Tesla-owned Austin Cybercab fleet has grown roughly tenfold since its recent launch; the company also plans to introduce the vehicle in Dallas next month. Notably, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration still has an open inquiry into how the steering-wheel-free vehicle complies with federal motor vehicle safety standards.

Rivian Acquires Simulation Startup; Lucid Advances European Robotaxi Plans

Rivian announced Thursday that it has acquired Third Dimension AI, a UK-based startup that turns real-world images and video into controllable high-fidelity 3D environments. Terms were not disclosed. The 15-person team will join Rivian’s autonomy and AI group. The deal is intended to accelerate synthetic data generation and simulation for Rivian’s driver-assistance systems and the self-driving software for robotaxis it plans to supply to Uber, the company said.

European self-driving company Bolt, meanwhile, said its planned fleet of at least 25,000 autonomous Lucid vehicles in Europe will use Nvidia’s Alpamayo Stack to enable autonomous driving. The robotaxi program is set to begin with data-collection vehicles in Madrid in 2027, subject to regulatory approval, before expanding to other markets such as Germany and France.

GM Details Fourth-Generation EV Platform; Ford Updates Mustang Mach-E

General Motors this week outlined its fourth-generation EV platform, which will use lithium manganese-rich (LMR) prismatic cells exclusively for high-volume EV segments. The company said the chemistry is designed to deliver about 33% more energy density than lithium iron phosphate at a comparable cost, supporting roughly 20% more range per kilowatt-hour. The platform also features simpler drive units with about 40% fewer parts. Production of the LMR cells is targeted for 2028.

Ford, meanwhile, opened orders for the 2027 model year Mustang Mach-E electric SUV, which now includes a standard extended-range battery and starts under $40,000. The Mustang Mach-E seeks to rival Tesla’s best-selling Model Y.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA was 'bearish' at the time of writing, while sentiment around RIVN, F, and LCID was 'neutral,' and sentiment around GM was 'extremely bullish.'

data.title: Soy basis steady-weaker after active week of harvest
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans were mostly steady to softer in the US Midwest on Friday after a week of active harvesting sent fresh supplies of the oilseed into marketing channels, grain merchandisers said.

  • The spot soybean basis fell by 10 cents a bushel at a Toledo, Ohio, terminal and by 5 cents at an elevator in Council Bluffs, Iowa.

  • However, the bean basis improved by 5 cents at a Morris, Illinois, elevator on the Illinois River, where grain is loaded onto barges for shipment toward Gulf Coast exporters.

  • The CIF basis for soybeans at the Gulf has strengthened this week following a series of US soybean export sales to China.

  • Farmers were aggressively harvesting soybeans and corn this week under mostly clear skies. Some growers in Iowa and Indiana were nearly finished with soybeans and were moving on to harvesting corn, merchandisers said this week.

  • Corn basis bids were flat on Friday afternoon, spot checks showed, but values strengthened earlier this week at a few locations, reflecting demand from grain handlers and a slow pace of farmer selling as Chicago Board of Trade corn futures (CZ26) hovered near three-month lows.

  • Farmers had sold corn as futures rallied to multiyear highs in late August and September, analysts said, and some were inclined to store the rest of their output in hopes of a rally down the road.

  • CBOT December corn futures settled down 4-1/2 cents on Friday at $4.56 per bushel while November soybeans (SX26) ended up 3-1/2 cents at $12.56-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training after security overhaul, discloses flaw in widely used software
data.description:
OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while testing its defenses.

The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them.

OpenAI had paused training of its most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error to gain limited internet access in September. The company said it contained the incident and used the pause to strengthen its defenses.

To test them, OpenAI had teams of AI agents try to break out of their restricted environments. It said the agents found previously unknown flaws, which it had fixed, and training resumed on October 1.

During that exercise, the ChatGPT maker found a flaw in Brotli, a widely used data compression tool.

The company said attackers could exploit the flaw by sending malicious data that lets them run their own code on affected systems, including those using popular web software such as Node.js, Bun and Envoy.

OpenAI said the root cause was fixed in Brotli's source code in February, before it was known to create a security vulnerability, but no new version was released at the time. Brotli has since released updated versions and published a public record of the flaw after OpenAI disclosed it.

Separately on Thursday, AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research said they found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year.

OpenAI told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes.

OpenAI has been conducting a broad review of its AI models' activity since the Hugging Face incident in July, and has informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents.

data.title: UK's Healey to give two state-backed lenders £20 billion capital boost in budget
data.description:
Britain will provide £20.4 billion ($27.3 billion) of additional capital to the state's business lender and infrastructure bank in next week's budget, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing the Treasury.

  • The Treasury will allocate £15.4 billion ($20.6 billion) more to the National Wealth Fund and £5 billion ($7 billion) more to the British Business Bank over roughly half a decade, according to the report.

  • "This additional capital will help more British businesses fulfil their potential, while getting investment behind the industries, infrastructure and places that create good jobs and drive lasting growth across the country," a Treasury spokesperson told the FT.

  • The Treasury did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.

  • The Treasury said the funding would help support around 100,000 jobs by 2035 in sectors including artificial intelligence, defence and green energy, the FT said.

  • The measures are expected to be announced in finance minister John Healey's budget on Wednesday.

data.title: Stocktwits Defense Watch: Lockheed Martin, RTX, L3Harris, HII Add To Their Defense Contract Backlogs Amid Pentagon Spending Ramp-Up
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lockheed Martin reached a preliminary agreement with the Department of War to manufacture and maintain 850 F-35 fighter jets over the next decade.
  • RTX and Lockheed Martin’s Javelin joint venture received a $215 million U.S. Army contract.
  • Raytheon secured an additional $394 million Missile Defense Agency contract.

Defense contractors secured a fresh wave of military contracts and long-term production commitments this week, as the U.S.-Iran war neared the end of its eighth month and fears of renewed military strikes kept the spotlight on America's defense capabilities.

Tensions remained high this week as U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly weighed an immediate end to the war, while Tehran warned of broader retaliation across the Middle East if U.S. and Israeli strikes resumed.

Against this backdrop, Lockheed Martin (LMT) unveiled a major 10-year F-35 production framework, while L3Harris Technologies (LHX), RTX (RTX) and HII (HII) were awarded new contracts spanning electronic warfare, missile defense and naval operations.

Lockheed Martin Reaches Major F-35 Agreement

On Thursday, Lockheed Martin and the Department of War (DOW) reached a preliminary agreement to produce and support at least 850 F-35 fighter jets over the next decade.

The agreement aims to maintain annual production of 156 aircraft and strengthen the supply chain for the stealth fighter program. Lockheed will invest at least $7 billion of its own funds to support the initiative. However, the agreement is not yet a finalized aircraft order, with pricing and delivery schedules still subject to further negotiations and approvals.

Separately, Lockheed Martin reported an 11% growth in third-quarter (Q3) revenue, which also came above Wall Street’s estimate of $20.46 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share rose to $7.97 from $6.95 a year earlier, beating expectations of $7.52 per share.

The defense behemoth raised its full-year (FY) 2026 revenue guidance to $80 billion to $82 billion, and earnings outlook to $30.35 - $30.75 per share from $29.95 - $30.65.

L3Harris Wins $876M Navy Award

On Monday, L3Harris Technologies received an $876.4 million contract from the U.S. Navy on Monday for the Next Generation Jammer Low Band program. The system is designed to help military aircraft disrupt radar and communications.

Separately, L3Harris opened a new solid rocket motor manufacturing facility in Arkansas on Tuesday, with the aim of doubling its existing production capacity.

RTX, Lockheed Secure Javelin Orders

RTX’s unit, Raytheon, and Lockheed Martin secured a $215 million U.S. Army contract to manufacture next-generation launchers for Javelin anti-tank missiles on Monday. The new unit is 30% smaller and 25% lighter than the previous version, while offering twice the target detection and recognition capability, the companies said.

The award follows the first deliveries of the upgraded launchers in May.

RTX also received a $394 million contract extension from the Missile Defense Agency to maintain and support AN/TPY-2 missile-defense radar systems through October 2028. The extension also raises the existing contract ceiling to about $3 billion.

HII Gets $99M Navy Shipbuilding Work

HII secured a $99 million U.S. Navy contract modification to conduct sea trials for the Lyndon B. Johnson destroyer ship on Monday. This is an extension of an existing contract with work expected to continue through October 2028.

The destroyer is also being upgraded to carry the Navy’s Conventional Prompt Strike hypersonic missile system, designed to strike distant targets at extremely high speeds.

How Did LMT, RTX, HII And LHX Fare This Week?

Lockheed Martin led the gains this week with a 10.6% gain, followed by L3Harris at 3.7% and HII at 1.7%, while RTX was the only laggard in this cohort, down about 0.5%.

LMT was also far and away the biggest gainer so far this year, rising about 22%. RTX was up 2.2% while LHX slumped 17% and HII tanked 22%.

data.title: Stocktwits Fintech Pulse: US Fintech Weekly Briefing And Market Drivers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Payment providers received price target increases from Truist, while reports suggested Visa was in talks to acquire stablecoin firm Fireblocks.
  • Fiserv expanded partnerships with Klarna and VikingCloud during the week.
  • The Securities and Exchange Commission approved a landmark Cboe Exchange rule change enabling cash-settled binary options.

Domestic card networks and payment processors saw positive broker sentiment and strategic risk upgrades, while Fiserv’s new partnerships and the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) approval around binary options contracts were the fintech highlights for the week of Oct. 19 to Oct. 23.

Investor attention would now shift to the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy meeting due next week to judge the future course on interest rates and its effect on fintech and lending stocks, with elevated oil prices continuing to weigh on inflation projections. Market participants are currently betting on a 91% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged next week.

Infrastructure Shifts Across Mastercard, Visa, PayPal, and Fiserv 

Mastercard Incorporated (MA): Mastercard introduced a new risk intelligence protocol on Oct. 19 designed to bolster transaction security across global stablecoin payment rails.

Meanwhile, analysts at Truist raised the firm's price target on MasterCard to $674 from $633 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares. “The US macro backdrop remains constructive, though the firm is wary of a slowdown in European consumer spending and the adverse impact of higher rates, the analyst told investors in a research note accessed by TheFly.

Visa Inc. (V): Visa is in late-stage talks to acquire stablecoin infrastructure and custody company Fireblocks for about $2.5 billion, Axios reported, citing multiple sources. However, Fireblocks denied Axios’ report. Truist Securities also hiked its target price on Visa to to $443 from $406.

Fiserv, Inc. (FISV): Fiserv unveiled a multi-year partnership with cybersecurity firm VikingCloud to enhance merchant threat protection and streamline PCI compliance efforts. Starting in early 2027, the payment processor will integrate VikingCloud Cyber Risk Defense, providing clients with continuous monitoring capabilities and actionable risk mitigation insights.

Additionally, Klarna (KLAR) is joining Fiserv’s Commerce Hub platform. The integration enables enterprise merchants across North America, the UK, and Europe to deliver Klarna’s payment options across both digital and physical retail locations.

How Neobank SoFi Performed 

While Truist was bullish on payment operators, the research firm cut down its price target on SoFi this week to to $16 from $19.

Meanwhile, the neobank partnered with Prudential Financial (PRU) to let over 15 million SoFi members purchase Prudential term life insurance directly in the SoFi app. Eligible members are will be able to obtain coverage in minutes without a medical exam or lab work.

Shares of SoFi ended the week higher after it fell nearly 8% in the previous week amid selling pressure tied to higher interest rates. Investors would be keenly watching the firm’s deposit growth during its official earnings call on Oct. 27.

Analysts Turn Bullish On Robinhood

JPMorgan raised the firm's price target on Robinhood to $115 from $103 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, while Rosenblatt initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating on the firm.

“Few companies can claim to have changed an entire industry, but what started as a commission-free trading app has become a full financial platform, and the market still under-appreciates how much the story has matured,” Rosenblatt told investors in a research note, accessed by TheFly.

However, last week, Wells Fargo lowered Robinhood's price target to $120 from $125 and kept an ‘Equal Weight’ rating on the shares. Meanwhile, founder and CEO Vlad Tenev sold nearly $43 million in company stock, but Barron's reported he’s far from cashing out.

HOOD stock ended the week nearly 4% lower, its fifth straight week of decline and the longest weekly losing streak since January this year.

Federal Rules And Legal Updates 

The SEC approved a Cboe Exchange proposal to list binary options tied to public company key performance indicators (KPIs). The contracts pay out based on whether quarterly metrics reported in Form 8-K or 10-Q filings meet specified strike levels.

KPIs include balance sheet and income statement indicators, valuation metrics like price-to-equity (P/E) ratio, and regulatory disclosures.

data.title: Elon Musk Eyes SpaceX-Tesla Merger, Huang Pitches ‘Financeable’ Chips, Zuckerberg Wants More Compute: Mag 7 Voices This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • In the SpaceX earnings call, Elon Musk said a merger with Tesla would be a good idea, but warned that it would be “overstating it” to assume the deal was certain.
  • He also said that power and cooling, not chips, limit AI deployment, which led to a surge in Bloom Energy, Vertiv, and other power stocks.
  • Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he wants lenders to treat Nvidia chips as a “financeable asset,” pegged neocloud demand to be off “off the charts”, but warned that capital is scarce.

SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk was the most vocal market participant among the Magnificent Seven leaders this week with earnings of both his companies on deck.

Meta Platforms (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg also made headlines following Meta’s results, while Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang took the stage at GTC Berlin.

While all three offered a bullish view of AI demand, their comments also flagged the infrastructure and financing required to keep up with it. Musk pointed to power and cooling as bigger constraints on AI deployment than chips, while Huang stated that Nvidia’s computing hardware should become a “financeable asset,” and Zuckerberg said Meta’s AI assistant Muse was only limited by a shortage of computing capacity.

The market was less forgiving. The Nasdaq Composite had its worst session since June on Thursday as concerns about AI spending and higher oil prices weighed on chip stocks.

Musk Backs SpaceX-Tesla Merger: Says Power, Not Chips, Limits AI

Musk used SpaceX’s third-quarter (Q3) earnings call on Tuesday to endorse a potential merger with Tesla, while cautioning that a deal remained uncertain.

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes.”

– Elon Musk, CEO, SpaceX and Tesla, on a possible merger

Musk said he felt like he was “tap dancing through a minefield,” when asked about the merger. He shared that the boards of both companies have formed special committees of independent directors, but the committees have not agreed on any terms. According to him, treating a merger as a certainty would be “overstating it.”

SpaceX’s Super Intelligence (SI) segment, which rents computing capacity and operates Grok, generated $7.6 billion in revenue, surpassing Starlink as the company’s largest business. According to Musk, the obstacle facing broad superintelligence deployment is securing enough power, cooling, and supporting infrastructure, rather than obtaining semiconductors.

“More in power and cooling and infrastructure than it is in chips.”

– Elon Musk, CEO, SpaceX and Tesla, on what constrains AI deployment

He said that SpaceX plans to add about 20 gigawatts of power and cooling capacity by the end of 2027, drawing on “many different sources of power, not just gas turbines.” Musk also flagged delays of 12 to 18 months for some gas-turbine components. He stated that the company’s plans were highly proprietary and did not identify suppliers.

Investors took notice of the infrastructure implications, with shares of Bloom Energy (BE), Vertiv (VRT), and other power companies rallying the following day. GE Vernova (GEV), Vistra (VST) and Constellation Energy (CEG) also gained Wednesday, according to Stocktwits.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock shifted to 'bearish' from 'bullish' over the past week, while chatter stayed at 'high' levels.

Tesla’s results also put autonomy and robotics in focus. Musk said the Cybercab fleet in Austin had grown tenfold since its launch about a month earlier and that robotaxis should begin contributing to the company’s financial results in 2027.

“I remain convinced that Optimus will be the biggest product on Earth.”

– Elon Musk, CEO, SpaceX and Tesla, on Optimus potential

Jensen Huang Sees AI Funding Squeeze

At GTC Berlin, Huang said Nvidia was working to persuade lenders to treat its chips as collateral, adding that computing capacity can be financed like other productive assets. According to him, compute holds value because it is fungible, productive, and durable.

“One of the things that we’re trying to do is to establish Nvidia’s compute as a financeable asset.”

– Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, to CNBC on the sidelines of GTC Berlin

Huang also remained bullish on demand for neocloud providers, which offer computing capacity to companies developing and running AI models. However, he flagged financing as the key limiting factor.

“If you look at the fundamentals, the demand for the neoclouds is off the charts. Their capabilities are extraordinary, and so what is missing in the middle is the working capital to fuel that growth, to fund that growth.”

– Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, to CNBC on the sidelines of GTC Berlin

According to him, capital is falling short because so many AI sectors are competing for it. He added that neoclouds need to “scale” in order to establish “regional excellence.”

Meanwhile, markets focused on the funding implications of Huang’s remarks. Wedbush said his comments on neocloud financing helped spark Thursday’s selloff.

On stage at GTC, Huang put the cost of a one-gigawatt AI factory at about $50 billion, including land, power, the building shell, computing equipment, networking, storage and cooling.

“Each gigawatt data center is $50 billion.”

– Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, at GTC Berlin

He estimated that such a facility could generate roughly $40 billion in annual revenue. A three-month delay would therefore cost about $10 billion, he said, adding that this “will make anybody anxious.”

Huang also predicted that telecommunications companies would become distributed AI networks, combining their cellular infrastructure with computing capacity. T-Mobile (TMUS) completed what Nvidia and Nokia (NOK) described as the first AI-RAN call on a live commercial network last week.

“Every single telco in the future, and I predict this, every single telco in the future, with 100,000 sites representing some 100 gigawatts of distributed telco base stations and data centers, will in the future evolve into a distributed AI network.”

– Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, at GTC Berlin

The comments came as Nvidia launched DSX POD, a containerized reference design for Vera Rubin AI factories that the company says can be deployed in as little as 14 days. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVDA stock shifted to 'bullish' from 'neutral' over the past week, while chatter stayed at 'normal' levels.

Mark Zuckerberg Says Meta’s AI Ambitions Are Constrained By Compute Shortages

During Meta’s earnings call, Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had signed up for Muse, Meta’s AI assistant. According to him, the company has not launched the service globally because it is compute-intensive.

“There is just nowhere near enough compute for all the demand.”

– Mark Zuckerberg, CEO, Meta, on Muse

Zuckerberg added that Meta expects Muse to serve billions of people and plans to begin monetizing the service sooner than it typically would for a new product. The company also announced a nonvoting Class C share and a two-for-one stock split expected in late January. The structure would allow Zuckerberg to retain control while the company continues funding its AI ambitions.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around META stock soared to 'extremely bullish' from 'bearish' over the past week, while chatter rose to 'high' from 'low' levels.

Satya Nadella Looks Beyond AI Hype

In an interview with Semafor this week, Nadella said that the AI industry needs to focus less on novelty and more on systems that work predictably and reliably. He stated that frontier AI labs were “magical businesses,” but added that early success does not guarantee long-term leadership in the industry.

“It’s not about the shiny object and FOMO.”

– Satya Nadella, CEO, Microsoft, to Semafor

Nadella’s annual letter, published the same day, placed AI agents at the center of Microsoft’s reorganization. He wrote that agents allow users to “macro delegate and micro steer,” and said Microsoft 365 Copilot had passed 30 million paid seats.

Sundar Pichai Prioritizes DeepMind’s Compute Needs

Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) CEO Sundar Pichai said this week that Google Cloud was giving up some short-term revenue so DeepMind could have first claim on computing capacity.

“Non-negotiable.”

– Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet, on DeepMind’s computing needs, on the Big Technology Podcast

Pichai said meeting requests from new customers seeking computing capacity for 2027 would be extremely difficult. He did not disclose how much revenue Alphabet was forgoing to prioritize DeepMind.

OpenAI began rolling out its models on Google Cloud in private preview on Wednesday. Pichai confirmed that Apple uses Gemini models in Siri and said the partnership was “working well.”

Amazon (AMZN) was largely absent from this week’s AI discussion, with CEO Andy Jassy making no new public remarks. Apple (AAPL) CEO John Ternus also did not make any fresh public comments this week.

data.title: US Metro Bancorp Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
US Metro Bancorp (): US Metro Bancorp (“Bancorp”) is a bank holding company, with a single subsidiary, US Metro Bank (“Bank”). On a consolidated basis, Bancorp earned $3.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. For the nine months ending September 30, 2026, the consolidated Bancorp earned $9.9 million compared to $8.0 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. On a year-to-date basis, Bancorp recorded an annualized return on average assets (“ROAA”) of 0.80% and an annualized return on average equity (“ROAE”) of 11.32%. With 16,791,500 shares outstanding, earnings per share (“EPS”) for the third quarter of 2026 was $0.19 compared to $0.21 in the second quarter of 2026. For the nine months ending September 30, 2026, EPS was $0.59 compared to $0.48 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. On September 30, 2026, Bancorp’s book value per share was $7.06 compared to $6.62 a year earlier.

The Bank recorded on a year-to-date basis net interest income of $39.9 million compared to $33.1 million in the same period a year earlier. Net income of $11.7 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $9.2 million reported for the same nine months in 2025, a year over year increase of $2.55 million.

The Bank reported total assets of $1.730 billion as of September 30, 2026, representing a 10.2% increase compared to the reporting period ending September 30, 2025, and year over year loan growth of $157 million or 12.4%. Total Bank deposits ended the third quarter of 2026 at $1.527 billion, a $143 million or 10.3% increase from $1.384 billion on September 30, 2025.

Non-performing assets as a percentage of total assets of 1.39% on September 30, 2026, compared to 1.46% as of September 30, 2025. The Bank had $2.3 million Other Real Estate Owned (OREO) on September 30, 2026. Allowance for credit losses (ACL) to gross loans was 1.25% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 1.19% as of September 30, 2025. The Bank recorded a $7.6 million provision for credit losses, for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $2.2 million recorded for the nine months ending September 30, 2025.

“Our third quarter results reflect the continued strength of our core franchise. Year-to-date earnings of $9.9 million are up 24% over the same period last year, and we delivered double-digit year-over-year growth in loans, deposits, and total assets. While the third quarter earnings were modestly below the second quarter, we continued to prudently build our allowance for credit losses, and we are encouraged by the improvement in non-performing assets compared to a year ago. With book value per share rising to $7.06, we remain focused on finishing 2026 strong and building long-term value for our shareholders,” said CEO Dong Il Kim.

US Metro Bank is a California chartered, full service commercial bank headquartered in Garden Grove, California. The Bank opened for business on September 15, 2006, and offers deposit and loan products (including commercial real estate, commercial and industrial, mortgage, SBA and USDA loans), as well as related banking services to its customers.

data.title: AI Hacks Are Coming Thick and Fast and Overwhelming the Internet — WSJ
data.description:
By Robert McMillan

The AI-powered hackers began stealing from Colin Parsons at 11 p.m. on a recent Friday night.

The next morning, the startup founder woke up to about 50 email messages, each one saying he had been charged a few more dollars for Anthropic and OpenAI's services. The bills ran to $449.

Parsons is just one of the latest victims in a wave of artificial-intelligence-powered attacks that has flooded the internet in recent weeks, as hackers increasingly turn to agents and AI hacking tools that make intrusions faster and harder to track than ever before.

"We've been seeing an explosion of these agentic adversaries," said Adam Meyers, a senior vice president with the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike. "We've found advanced adversaries using this; we've found very unsophisticated adversaries using this."

The sharp increase in hacks is part of a dizzying AI-driven acceleration of cybersecurity threats that is rippling around the world. At the same time as new tools speed up hackers, cyber defenders are also racing to fix the fast-growing volume of security bugs discovered by AI, before hackers can exploit the new flaws.

On Wednesday, organizations scrambled to patch newly uncovered bugs that could allow takeover of as many as 70% of the world's websites. Hackers are now actively trying to break into websites by leveraging these flaws, Amazon.com says.

The National Security Agency and Federal Bureau of Investigation have told companies that couldn't immediately patch the web bugs to simply pull the plug on their websites. Government-run sites in countries such as Canada, Belgium, France, the Netherlands did just that. The image-posting message board 4chan suspended comments on its site ahead of the patches.

The pace and volume of the AI-powered attacks are starting to overwhelm the incident-response firms that respond to cyber breaches. Pundits are referring to the month as "Black October," and many in the field are predicting more to come.

"We expect that there's going to be a massive number of compromise disclosures in the coming weeks and months," said Steven Adair, president of the cybersecurity firm Volexity.

Incident responders such as Adair say that AI tools are now being used by nation-state hackers from China and Russia as well as criminals looking to steal data and install ransomware.

One of the tools they are using is a Chinese open-source hacking tool called Artex, which uses artificial intelligence to automate the process of breaking into a computer network.

This week Microsoft said that "threat actors across multiple geographic regions" were using Artex to speed up attacks on hundreds of companies. Earlier this month, a cyberattack used Artex to steal data on about 68,000 people from South Korean banks.

Hackers are using AI for reconnaissance, to analyze vast swaths of data they steal and even to rapidly build exploit code that can be used to break into networks, said Sherri Davidoff, founder of the security consulting firm LMG Security.

Every three months, Davidoff works with a data-breach services company called NetDiligence to poll a group of her peers about the techniques they are seeing in real-world cyberattacks. A year ago, virtually none of them saw any signs of AI use. During the past quarter, it has become routine, she said.

Earlier this year, researchers at the cybersecurity firm Sophos gained access to systems used by a Russian-speaking ransomware group calling itself Aurora and they were able to observe things as the group evolved and became increasingly dependent on AI.

At first the hackers used AI to build tooling and infrastructure to host their ransomware attacks. By the year's end they were using it to sniff around corporate networks they had hacked into, looking for ways to break into other accounts.

The Russian ransomware group also shifted over the course of the year from proprietary models like Anthropic's to new open-source ones like the Kimi models from Moonshot AI, said Colin Cowie, manager of threat intelligence with Sophos.

"The pace that they operate at is faster than the average human," Cowie added.

The hackers accessed the AI models using a $200-per-month license from AI-coding service Cursor, Cowie said.

It isn't clear what specific tools Colin Parsons's hackers used, but they were looking for online credentials that could be used to obtain AI services.

Parsons's unauthorized purchases were made using credentials Parson had stored with an AI-coding site called OpenCode. Starting on Oct. 16, OpenCode was locked in a "non stop" AI-fueled cyberattack, the company's co-founder, Dax Raas said on X. Later he added, "damn we basically need agents going 24/7 because that's what they have."

OpenCode representatives didn't reply to messages seeking comment.

When Parsons fired up his Discord messaging app and went to OpenCode's customer support channel, it was flooded not with support queries but nonsensical messages saying things like, "Yo," or "Delete telegram." A new one would pop up every two seconds. When Parsons posted a note about the fraudulent charges, it was quickly buried by the nonsense.

He tagged OpenCode in a post on X, asking, "have you guys been hacked?"

Soon other OpenCode users said they had been hit too.

"Yep - same thing - $1700," wrote one.

"same here," wrote another.

"I'm very pissed off, my keys were leaked," a third said, adding that his OpenAI account was suspended.

data.title: Stocktwits Biotech Dealmaker: Gilead And Roche Double Down On Early-Stage Assets Over Full Buyouts This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gilead Sciences agreed on Thursday to buy Shanghai-based PepStar Therapeutics’ experimental oral drug program for inflammatory diseases. 
  • Roche gained exclusive global rights to Zymeworks’ ZW209 in a deal worth up to $813 million plus royalties.
  • Roche and Hansoh Pharma also expanded their antibody-drug conjugate partnership in a deal that could exceed $15 billion in total value.

Large drugmakers continued to favor targeted asset purchases and licensing deals for early-stage, differentiated candidates rather than full company acquisitions this week, implying a shift from earlier this year, when full-scale acquisitions dominated the sector.

Inflammation, cancer therapies called antibody-drug conjugates, and next-generation T-cell engagers with possibilities in treating cancer drew the biggest capital in the relatively slow week for biotech dealmaking, as companies sought to fill specific pipeline gaps. The sole exception was Merck KGaA’s roughly $1.3 billion purchase of Silence Therapeutics.

Gilead Acquires Oral Drug Program For $1.275B

Gilead Sciences (GILD) agreed on Thursday to buy Shanghai-based PepStar Therapeutics’ experimental oral drug program for inflammatory diseases, including its lead candidate HCXT-2001, for $1.275 billion in cash.

Gilead sees potential to develop the early-stage asset alone or in combination with its own oral drug emvistegrast as an all-oral approach for inflammatory bowel disease. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter and gives Gilead worldwide rights. The deal comes as part of Gilead’s efforts to expand its inflammation portfolio beyond its core HIV business and follows a mid-October collaboration deal with Vir Biotechnology.

Roche Licenses Zymeworks' Drug For Lung Cancer

U.S.-listed shares of Switzerland-based Roche (RHHBY) gained exclusive global rights to Zymeworks’ (ZYME) ZW209 in a deal worth up to $813 million plus royalties. Zymeworks will receive $55 million upfront and $40 million upon initiation of a Phase 1b trial, with eligibility for up to $718 million in additional development, commercial, and sales milestones, plus tiered high-single-digit to mid-teen royalties.

Zymeworks will run the Phase 1a monotherapy study with Roche funding, after which Roche takes over global development and commercialization. The candidate targets DLL3, a protein commonly expressed on small-cell lung cancer cells.

Roche Expands ADC Collaboration With Hansoh

Roche and China-based pharmaceutical company Hansoh Pharma also expanded their antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) partnership in a deal that could exceed $15 billion in total value. Hansoh will receive $400 million upfront and $110 million on the first anniversary, plus eligibility for more than $15 billion in development, regulatory, and commercialization milestones, along with royalties.

The collaboration covers two preclinical Hansoh ADC programs and multiple additional programs against Roche-selected targets using Hansoh’s platform. Hansoh will lead development through global Phase 1a trials. Roche then takes over worldwide development outside Greater China, where Hansoh retains rights. The agreement builds on a prior single-asset ADC partnership and underscores Roche’s continued push into next-generation ADCs across multiple cancer types.

Merck KGaA To Acquire Silence Therapeutics For $1.3B

Merck KGaA on Monday agreed to acquire Silence Therapeutics (SLN) in an all-cash deal with an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The German drugmaker will pay $20 per American Depositary Share, representing a roughly 130% premium to the stock’s close before the deal announcement.

The main prize is divesiran, a late-stage-ready therapy for a rare blood cancer. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 and adds both a late-stage rare-disease asset and RNA technology to Merck’s pipeline.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GILD was 'neutral' at the time of writing, while sentiment around RHHBY, ZYME, and SLN was 'bullish' or 'extremely bullish.'

data.title: SpaceX’s 80,000 Cell Site Push A Win For ASTS, Ericsson, Nokia, NextNav, Among Others, Says Roth Capital
data.description:
Key points:
  • Scotiabank upgraded AST SpaceMobile to Outperform from Sector Perform and lifted its price target to $55.70 from $50.80.
  • Citi analysts characterized the development as a net positive for tower operators Crown Castle, SBA Communications and American Tower. 
  • In an October 20 meeting with FCC officials, major U.S. wireless carriers asked the agency to keep two key 5G spectrum bands out of draft rules that would expand satellite-to-phone service.

Roth Capital analyst Scott Searle said SpaceX’s reported interest in leasing tower capacity at as many as 80,000 sites could benefit a range of equipment, backhaul, and spectrum names as the company builds out a complementary terrestrial network to support its direct-to-device satellite constellation and challenge existing U.S. mobile carriers.

Searle pointed to AST SpaceMobile (ASTS), radio-access-network suppliers Ericsson (ERIC) and Nokia (NOK), wireless backhaul providers Aviat Networks (AVNW) and Ceragon Networks (CRNT), and spectrum holders Anterix (ATEX), NextNav (NN) and Gogo (GOGO) as potential winners of any such buildout.

The analyst was responding to a report from Bloomberg on Thursday that SpaceX is pursuing agreements for a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the United States as it advances plans to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier.

The report said that SpaceX is in discussions with at least one major cellular infrastructure company and said Crown Castle Inc. (CCI), among the largest U.S. owners of cellular towers alongside American Tower (AMT) and Vertical Bridge, was also approached for the purpose.

Scotiabank Upgrades ASTS, Citi Sees Downside For Carriers

Scotiabank, meanwhile, upgraded AST SpaceMobile to 'Outperform' from 'Sector Perform' and lifted its price target to $55.70 from $50.80. The analyst argued that SpaceX’s broader ambition to operate as a planetary carrier increases the strategic value of AST’s wholesale 5G model for terrestrial networks seeking to protect their core business. With the stock down roughly 70% since May, Scotiabank described the current valuation as reasonably attractive and potentially a bargain.

Citi analysts, meanwhile, characterized the development as a net positive for tower operators Crown Castle, SBA Communications and American Tower, and as negative for the major wireless carriers. The analysts estimated valuation risk of 29% to 32% for AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon, with a further 4 % to 16% downside from current levels following the stocks’ declines in 2026.

Meanwhile, Telecom Operators Push Back Against SpaceX

In an October 20 meeting with FCC officials, major U.S. wireless carriers asked the agency to keep two key 5G spectrum bands out of draft rules that would expand satellite-to-phone service. The carriers, through their trade group CTIA, said the changes would create interference risks for existing networks used by more than 300 million people.

They also asked the FCC to keep current rules that require satellite operators to reach agreements with the carriers before using their licensed spectrum, and to hold satellite services to the same standards as traditional wireless networks. The request comes ahead of a possible FCC vote on the draft rules later this month.

SpaceX, meanwhile, is seeking to establish itself as a standalone wireless competitor and recently acquired low-band spectrum that will help integrate its Starlink satellites into what CEO Elon Musk has described as a “major mobile carrier.”

data.title: Boeing supplier dispute has halted 777 freighter production for two months, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Price dispute with supplier stops Boeing 777 freighter production
  • Boeing wants to take over production of the parts in question, sources say
  • 777X jets avoid impact because their wings are made of composites

By Dan Catchpole

Boeing's dispute with a small Florida-based supplier has halted production of its 777 freighter for nearly two months and disrupted output of the 767, including freighters and KC-46 aerial refueling tankers, according to Boeing workers and court filings.

Boeing filed a complaint in August alleging supplier Vaero had stopped delivering a critical wing component known as the trailing-edge rib kit, stalling work at the Everett, Washington, wing-production facility that supports the 777 freighter and 767 programs, according to a copy of the complaint reviewed by Reuters. The disruption was costing Boeing as much as $6.5 million a day, the complaint said.

Boeing said in the complaint that the trailing-edge rib kit was an "indispensable" part and Vaero was the sole supplier.

Although the companies reached a settlement in late September, production of the 777 freighter has yet to resume, according to three Boeing workers familiar with the matter. They declined to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

The dispute also disrupted production of the 767, a widebody cargo and military aircraft, the people said. Since the settlement, Boeing has received some parts for the 767 line, according to one of the workers.

The prolonged disruption highlights the fragility of aerospace supply chains, showing how a dispute involving a single supplier can halt production of aircraft that remain in strong demand.

The lawsuit was first reported by Law.com in August, but the nearly two-month production disruption has not previously been reported.

Boeing declined to comment. Vaero did not respond to requests for comment.

BRINGING PRODUCTION IN-HOUSE

Boeing is trying to bring production of the trailing-edge rib kit in-house, according to two of the people. The component is used in wing assembly for the 767 and current-generation 777 freighter. Boeing's 777X, which uses composite wings, has not been affected.

Without the Vaero parts, Boeing removed two partially assembled 777 freighters from its final assembly line, according to one Boeing worker.

Using data from aviation consultancy IBA, Reuters identified one of the aircraft as destined for FedEx .

FedEx did not respond to a request for comment.

Boeing has delivered 21 777 freighters so far this year, company data show. It also has a handful of freighters whose wings were assembled before the dispute and could still be delivered before year-end, according to two of the Boeing workers.

data.title: Middle East physical oil prices are falling while Brent crude soars to six-month highs
data.description:
Physical prices of some Middle East crudes sold outside the Persian Gulf reportedly have dropped in recent days, as more cargoes are pushed through the Strait of Hormuz in ship-to-ship transfers offshore Oman and producers offer competitive prices to Asian buyers.

Among examples of the shift, a cargo of Iraqi Basrah Medium crude was sold at a discount of nearly $10/bbl to the physical Dubai benchmark on a ship-to-ship transfer basis in the Gulf of Oman, after the crude grade was offered at near parity to Dubai a month ago, traders told Bloomberg.

The premium of Oman crude over Dubai, the leading Middle East measure of market strength, fell this week to the lowest level since the end of July, according to OilPrice.com, after the differential had surged to as high as $65/bbl in March.

The higher availability is depressing the prices of various physical crude grades from the Middle East, which come with assurances of an ability to get oil out of the Gulf, and are in contrast with trends in global benchmark oil futures, with front-month Brent contracts rising for five consecutive weeks and settling at six-month highs on Friday.

"The move higher in oil futures is not fundamentally driven at the moment; instead the market is trading supply risks," ING's head of commodities strategy Warren Patterson said in a note.

"While Middle East flows are holding up well for now, the real concern for the market is how sustainable these would be with renewed attacks, which helps to explain the divergence between the paper and physical market," Patterson said.

Meanwhile, a tanker carrying Russian diesel is heading to the U.S., Reuters reported Friday, following the agreement reached this month between the two countries.

The Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes ​was loaded with 40K metric tons of ultra-low sulfur diesel in the Russian Baltic port of ​Primorsk on October 22 and is expected to arrive in the U.S. on November 7, according to the report.

The cargo will be the first ​imported by the U.S. since former President Biden announced a ban on U.S. imports ​of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022.

Crude oil futures rose Friday, closing out the week with strong gains on fears of escalating conflict in the Middle East driven by Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and increasing talk about renewed U.S. military strikes against Iran.

"Crude oil prices are on the rise as the market rebuilds geopolitical risk premium amid escalatory rhetoric from the U.S.-Israel and Iran, raising fears of renewed and potentially even more intense back-and-forth strikes," Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note.

"The market is concerned about the continued Iranian attacks on tankers that we've seen increase over the last week," according to Lipow Oil Associates president Andrew Lipow. "While there has been an increase in oil transiting out of the Strait of Hormuz, that could change at any minute."

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude for December delivery rallied 3.8% to $103.27 and front-month Brent crude for December delivery surged 3.1% to $116.72/bbl, its highest settlement value since April 29.

data.title: Travere Presents New Biomarker Data at ASN Kidney Week Suggesting FILSPARI® (sparsentan) May Modify Underlying Disease Pathophysiology in IgA Nephropathy
data.description:
Travere Therapeutics, Inc. () today presented new biomarker data from the Phase 3 PROTECT Study providing evidence that FILSPARI® (sparsentan) may modify the underlying disease pathophysiology in people with IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Data were shared today in an oral presentation at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, CO.

“These biomarker data provide new insight into how FILSPARI’s dual mechanism of action may modify the underlying biology of IgA nephropathy,” said Jula Inrig, M.D., chief medical officer of Travere Therapeutics. “When considered alongside the PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan, as well as published real-world evidence showing consistent outcomes in clinical practice, the totality of evidence supports the use of FILSPARI as a non-immunosuppressive, kidney-targeted, foundational first-line treatment for IgA nephropathy.”

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of FILSPARI, compared to irbesartan in 404 adult patients with IgAN. Of the overall study population, 295 patients participated in the biomarker analysis. Across measured time points through Week 110, FILSPARI led to rapid and sustained reductions in all four urinary biomarkers evaluated.

“These findings extend the exploratory signal observed in SPARTAN and show in a larger, randomized study that dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may modulate several biological pathways associated with IgAN pathophysiology,” said Chee Kay Cheung, M.B.Ch.B., Ph.D., consultant nephrologist at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust.

At Week 110, least-squares mean percent changes from baseline, normalized to urine creatinine, were greater with FILSPARI than with irbesartan (reported p values are nominal):

  • sCD163, a marker of macrophage activation, decreased 60.1% with FILSPARI versus 26.0% with irbesartan, representing a 46.1% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).
  • BAFF, a marker of B-cell activation and survival, decreased 64.4% with FILSPARI versus 45.2% with irbesartan, representing a 34.9% difference between treatment arms (p=0.02).
  • C5b-9, a marker of complement pathway activation, decreased 50.2% with FILSPARI versus 7.3% with irbesartan, representing a 46.3% difference between treatment arms (p=0.032).
  • IL-6, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, decreased 45.4% with FILSPARI versus an 8.7% increase with irbesartan, representing a 49.7% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).

The findings build on previously reported PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline with FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan. The consistency of effects across clinical outcomes and multiple biomarkers associated with IgAN disease biology provides further evidence that FILSPARI’s dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may provide benefits beyond conventional RAS inhibition and supports its differentiated profile as an early, foundational, non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgAN.

More information on Travere’s presence at ASN Kidney Week can be found here.

About the PROTECT Study

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan in 404 adults with biopsy-confirmed IgAN. Participants had urine protein excretion (UPE) ≥1.0 g/d and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² despite optimized renin-angiotensin system inhibitor therapy. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive FILSPARI 400 mg/day or irbesartan 300 mg/day for up to 110 weeks. The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in proteinuria from baseline at Week 36, and the key secondary efficacy endpoint was the rate of change in eGFR through Week 110.

About Travere Therapeutics

At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We are a biopharmaceutical company that comes together every day to help patients, families and caregivers of all backgrounds as they navigate life with a rare disease. On this path, we know the need for treatment options is urgent – that is why our global team works with the rare disease community to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies. In pursuit of this mission, we continuously seek to understand the diverse perspectives of rare patients and to courageously forge new paths to make a difference in their lives and provide hope – today and tomorrow. For more information, visit travere.com.

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) U.S. Indication

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) is indicated:

  • To slow kidney function decline in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk for disease progression.
  • To reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

BOXED WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY AND EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Under the FILSPARI REMS, prescribers, patients and pharmacies must enroll in the program.

Hepatotoxicity

Some Endothelin Receptor Antagonists (ERAs) have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. In clinical studies, elevations in aminotransferases (ALT or AST) of at least 3-times the Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge.

Measure transaminases and bilirubin before initiating treatment and then every 3 months during treatment. Interrupt treatment and closely monitor patients who develop aminotransferase elevations more than 3x ULN.

FILSPARI should generally be avoided in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) at baseline because monitoring for hepatotoxicity may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

FILSPARI is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant patients. Therefore, in patients who can become pregnant, exclude pregnancy prior to initiation of FILSPARI. Advise use of effective contraception before the initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.

Contraindications

FILSPARI is contraindicated in patients who are pregnant. Do not coadminister FILSPARI with angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), ERAs, or aliskiren.

Warnings and Precautions

  • Hepatotoxicity: Elevations in ALT or AST of at least 3-fold ULN have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge. While no concurrent elevations in bilirubin >2-times ULN or cases of liver failure were observed in FILSPARI-treated patients in clinical trials, some ERAs have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. To reduce the risk of potential serious hepatotoxicity, measure serum aminotransferase levels and total bilirubin prior to initiation of treatment and then every 3 months during treatment.Advise patients with symptoms suggesting hepatotoxicity (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, fatigue, anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, fever, or itching) to immediately stop treatment with FILSPARI and seek medical attention. If aminotransferase levels are abnormal at any time during treatment, interrupt FILSPARI and monitor as recommended.Consider re-initiation of FILSPARI only when hepatic enzyme levels and bilirubin return to pretreatment values and only in patients who have not experienced clinical symptoms of hepatotoxicity. Avoid initiation of FILSPARI in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) because monitoring hepatotoxicity in these patients may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.
  • FILSPARI REMS: Due to the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Prescribers, patients, and pharmacies must be enrolled in the REMS program and comply with all requirements (www.filsparirems.com).
  • Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Based on data from animal reproduction studies, FILSPARI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant patient and is contraindicated during pregnancy. The available human data for ERAs do not establish the presence or absence of fetal harm related to the use of FILSPARI. Counsel patients who can become pregnant of the potential risk to a fetus. Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment with FILSPARI. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. Advise pre-pubertal females and/or their guardian(s) of the fetal risk and the need to use effective contraception once they reach reproductive potential. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.
  • Hypotension: Hypotension has been observed in patients treated with ARBs and ERAs and was observed in FILSPARI clinical studies. There was a greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events, some serious, including dizziness, in patients treated with FILSPARI compared to irbesartan. In patients at risk for hypotension, consider eliminating or adjusting other antihypertensive medications and maintaining appropriate volume status. If hypotension develops, despite elimination or reduction of other antihypertensive medications, consider a dose reduction or dose interruption of FILSPARI. A transient hypotensive response is not a contraindication to further dosing of FILSPARI, which can be given once blood pressure has stabilized.
  • Acute Kidney Injury: Monitor kidney function periodically. Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) can cause kidney injury. Patients whose kidney function may depend in part on the activity of the RAS (e.g., patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart failure, or volume depletion) may be at particular risk of developing acute kidney injury on FILSPARI. Consider withholding or discontinuing therapy in patients who develop a clinically significant decrease in kidney function while on FILSPARI.
  • Hyperkalemia: Monitor serum potassium periodically and treat appropriately. Patients with advanced kidney disease, taking concomitant potassium-increasing drugs (e.g., potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics), or using potassium-containing salt substitutes are at increased risk for developing hyperkalemia. Dosage reduction or discontinuation of FILSPARI may be required.
  • Fluid Retention: Fluid retention may occur with ERAs and has been observed in clinical studies with FILSPARI. FILSPARI has not been evaluated in patients with heart failure. If clinically significant fluid retention develops, evaluate the patient to determine the cause and the potential need to initiate or modify the dose of diuretic treatment then consider modifying the dose of FILSPARI.

Adverse Reactions

  • IgAN patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are hyperkalemia, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), peripheral edema, dizziness, anemia, and acute kidney injury.

data.title: Judge puts off decision on Charlie Kirk murder trial date, media reports
data.description:
By Andrew Hay

A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported.

At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defense lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. He set a new hearing for November 9, television station KUTV reported.

Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial.

Robinson's attorneys had asked for a late 2029 trial to give them time to challenge Utah's request for the death penalty, gather additional evidence and seek a change of venue, among other issues, according to a scheduling memo.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, sought a date of January 31, 2028 to start what they expect to be a 17-week trial, according to their scheduling memo.

In a separate filing, Erika Kirk said the defense request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and requested the trial start no later than October 4, 2027.

Shortly before Friday's hearing, President Donald Trump, with whom Kirk had been allied, slammed Graf's handling of the case in a social media post, saying it should be tried within a month and Graf was asking "questions that people already know the answer to."

Kirk was a polarizing figure in US politics. He was admired by conservatives for mobilizing young voters around his Christian and right-wing views. Opponents criticized his rhetoric on immigration, race, gender and other social issues.

Prosecutors allege Robinson targeted Kirk for his opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights.

Defense attorney Richard Novak has said Kirk spoke "hatefully" about people who did not have traditional gender identities or were not heterosexual, but there was no evidence Robinson opposed those views.
